name: Taichung
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Taichung: machine tool and precision suppliers, counterfeit and fraud exposure, and court record research.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Taichung, scoped from Nashville: background research on precision machinery and component suppliers, support for brand owners facing counterfeiting, and review of judgments from the Taichung District Court and the High Court's Taichung branch for counsel and compliance teams.
intro: Taichung is Taiwan's second most populous city, a position it reached in 2017, with more than 2.85 million residents in 2024 according to a city promotional publication. The present municipality was formed when Taichung County and Taichung City merged in 2010. Export processing zones established in the 1950s and 1960s seeded a precision machinery industry that now defines the region: the city's Economic Development Bureau says about 70 percent of Taiwan's precision machinery, machine tool and component factories are in the central region. Central Taiwan Science Park, Taichung Industrial Park, the Precision Machinery Innovation Technology Park and the Taichung Export Processing Zone form an industrial corridor served by Taichung Port, Taichung International Airport and the high speed rail.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Taichung because so many of their suppliers, contract manufacturers and component makers are there. Buyers and investors need to know who owns a machine tool or parts supplier, whether it is financially stable and whether it has been involved in litigation, fraud or trademark disputes. Brand owners face counterfeiting: Taichung prosecutors indicted a group led by a precision company manager in 2023 over watches falsely sold as Swiss-made, and in 2025 indicted 23 people over a counterfeit whisky ring. Fraud and money laundering through corporate accounts are recurring themes in local prosecutions. Machinery exports also raise end-use and diversion questions that compliance teams must document.

matters.title: Precision machinery supplier diligence
matters.text: Background research on machine tool builders, component makers and contract manufacturers in the Taichung industrial corridor before sourcing, investment or acquisition, covering registration details, directors and supervisors, related companies, published judgments and Chinese-language media, so buyers understand who stands behind a supplier.

matters.title: Counterfeit and false origin claims
matters.text: Supporting brand owners and counsel where goods are suspected of being counterfeit or falsely labelled as to origin, by researching the companies, managers and distribution channels involved and identifying prior prosecutions, as in Taichung cases involving falsely marketed Swiss watches and counterfeit whisky.

matters.title: Export diversion and end-use checks
matters.text: Research for compliance teams on distributors and purchasers of Taichung-made machinery and components, testing whether a buyer is a genuine end user, how it is connected to other companies and whether public records or media suggest diversion. Licensing and classification questions remain with trade counsel.

matters.title: Fraud and laundering counterparties
matters.text: Screening counterparties and payment recipients in central Taiwan against published judgments and reporting on fraud and laundering schemes, including cases where corporate bank accounts were opened for illicit funds, to support banks, payment firms and corporate treasury teams in their decisions.

matters.title: Supplier insolvency and asset research
matters.text: Assembling public information for creditors and counsel when a Taichung supplier fails or stops performing, including its directors' other business interests, related companies that may have received assets or orders, and litigation already filed, before recovery steps are taken through Taiwanese counsel.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Taichung
local_context.text: Civil, commercial and criminal cases arising in the city are heard at first instance by the Taichung District Court, with appeals going to the Taichung Branch of the Taiwan High Court. Published reporting shows the branch reviewing district court rulings in fraud and money laundering cases. Judgments from both courts are a core source for researching Taichung companies and individuals, and are read in Chinese with attention to anonymisation of party names.

local_context.title: Prosecutors and investigation bureau
local_context.text: The Taichung District Prosecutors Office investigates and indicts fraud, forgery, trademark, food safety and organised crime offences in the city, and the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau has a Taichung branch office. Their published indictments and statements, often reported in the English-language press, document schemes such as false origin labelling, counterfeit goods and the misuse of corporate bank accounts, and help identify individuals and companies of concern.

local_context.title: Industrial parks and processing zones
local_context.text: Taichung's industrial base is organised around designated parks: Central Taiwan Science Park with its Taichung and Houli sites, Taichung Industrial Park, the Precision Machinery Innovation Technology Park, the Shengang Fengzhou Technology Industrial Park and the Taichung Export Processing Zone. Each has its own administering body. Knowing where a supplier sits helps identify which authority's records and announcements may be relevant.

local_context.title: Port and logistics links
local_context.text: Taichung Port and Taichung International Airport are the city's international gateways, and the high speed rail station connects it with Taipei and Kaohsiung. For trade-related matters, shipping patterns through the port and the location of warehouses and logistics providers can be relevant to supply chain and diversion questions, researched through lawful commercial and open sources. No restricted customs data is accessed.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Taichung, TDSC starts by identifying what the client needs to rely on, whether a supplier's ownership, a distributor's end use, a counterfeiting network or a debtor's assets, and the Taiwanese records that bear on it. Research is conducted from Nashville using Ministry of Economic Affairs registration data, judgments of the Taichung courts, prosecutors' announcements and Chinese-language open sources, reviewed by Mandarin-reading researchers. Taiwan has no dedicated investigator licensing regime, but its criminal law restricts covert recording and surveillance, so field enquiries are only undertaken through qualified local professionals coordinated by TDSC with the client's Taiwanese counsel, who advise on the Personal Data Protection Act and evidential use.

faqs.q: Can you verify who owns a Taichung machine tool supplier?
faqs.a: We review the supplier's registration data, including registered capital, representative, directors and supervisors, and research related companies, judgments and Chinese-language media. Shareholders behind a company are not always visible in public registration data, so we state where ownership remains uncertain and identify documents counsel can request in the transaction.

faqs.q: How do you help a brand owner with counterfeits made around Taichung?
faqs.a: We research the companies, managers and online and retail channels linked to the goods, identify prior prosecutions or judgments involving the same people, and map related entities. Test purchases, evidence preservation and enforcement actions are handled by Taiwanese counsel and qualified local professionals, coordinated with the client.

faqs.q: Which court will hear a dispute with a Taichung company?
faqs.a: Unless a contract provides otherwise, first-instance civil and commercial litigation against a Taichung company is commonly heard by the Taichung District Court, with appeals to the Taiwan High Court's Taichung Branch. Jurisdiction depends on the contract and claim, and Taiwanese counsel should confirm it. We research published judgments in both courts.

faqs.q: Can you check a buyer of machinery for diversion risk?
faqs.a: We research the buyer's registration, ownership indicators, related companies, trading history visible in open sources and adverse reporting, and flag inconsistencies with its stated end use. This supports, but does not replace, the export control assessment made by the client's trade compliance team and counsel.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Taichung?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is based in Nashville, Tennessee, and has no office or staff in Taichung or elsewhere in Taiwan. Engagements touching the city are scoped and managed from Nashville, with qualified Taiwanese professionals and the client's local counsel engaged where field work or legal advice is needed.
